title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Page headed '4 / Modèle d'une forme 1-dimensionnelle'. Grothendieck sets up a purely combinatorial, point-set axiomatics for 1-dimensional 'forms' (graphs, arcs, curves) that never uses the real line. The data are a set L of 'lieux' (places) and a set S of 'segments'. Two maps are given: I ↦ Ĩ ⊂ L (the places on I) and I ↦ ∂I ∈ P_2(L) (the two endpoints), with ∂I ⊂ Ĩ. The interior is Ĩ° = Ĩ \ ∂I.

Axiom F1 (sub-segments from an endpoint, apparently labelled in the margin as an axiom of 'connexité'/uniqueness). Let ∂I = {x,y} and S_{I,x} = {J ∈ S : J̃ ⊂ Ĩ, x ∈ ∂J}. The map S_{I,x} → Ĩ\{x}, J ↦ (the other endpoint of J), is required to be bijective. So for every z ∈ Ĩ\{x} there is a unique sub-segment I_{x,z} with endpoints {x,z}. NB: I_{x,y} = I_{y,x} = I.

Divisibility condition (marginal 'F.r.'). Ĩ° ≠ ∅.

Cutting condition. For z ∈ Ĩ°, Ĩ_{x,z} ∩ Ĩ_{y,z} = {z}. Moreover, any J ⊂ I with z ∈ ∂J satisfies J̃ ⊂ Ĩ_{x,z} or J̃ ⊂ Ĩ_{y,z}.

Consequences drawn:
- Cor. 1*: every Ĩ is infinite (using divisibility). Iterated halving gives a strictly decreasing chain, since y ∉ Ĩ_{x,z}.
- Cor. 2: the two alternatives in the cutting condition are mutually exclusive, since J̃ has at least two points but the intersection is {z}.
- Cor. 3: on S_I = {J : J̃ ⊂ Ĩ}, the map J ↦ ∂J ∈ P_2(Ĩ) is (a) injective, and (b) its image contains every pair meeting ∂I.

The next page completes Cor. 3 for pairs in the interior via a 'betweenness' criterion and proves Cor. 4 (Ĩ = J̃ ⇒ I = J, so S ⊂ P(L)). It then defines branches at a place x as an equivalence relation on segments with endpoint x (germ equivalence) and the 'ordre' of x as the number of branches, i.e. the valence / Menger–Urysohn order.

Purpose: a 'tame', number-free synthetic definition of 1-dimensional topological forms, as part of the 1986 'Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques)' project. It descends from the 'topologie modérée' programme of Esquisse d'un programme. Combined with the previous page's notion of singular places and specialisation (y specialises x if x is interior and y an endpoint of a segment), the aim seems to be to recover a graph-like or stratified structure, with generic interior points specialising to singular vertices.
errors: Cor. 3a (injectivity) is not immediate from F1 as stated. It requires the cutting condition: for interior endpoints u,v, both J and J' lie on the same side of u, then apply F1 inside I_{x,u} or I_{y,u}. The argument works but is not written.
The covering condition Ĩ = Ĩ_{x,z} ∪ Ĩ_{y,z}, flagged with '!!!' on the previous page, is not included in the axioms on this page. Without it, extraneous places could sit on Ĩ outside both halves.

Cor. 1 depends on the divisibility condition, which is only added marginally. On the next page Grothendieck reconsiders not imposing divisibility, which would allow finite (combinatorial-graph) models; then Cor. 1 fails.
Minor: the text writes 'J ⊂ Ĩ_{y,z}' without the tilde on J.

ideas.what: Axiomatics of 1-dimensional spaces via a set of places and a set of 'segments' with endpoint maps, unique sub-segment from an endpoint, and cutting at interior points
ideas.modern_name: betweenness/interval structures; axiomatics of arcs, dendrites, pretrees, R-tree-like segment systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pasch/Hilbert (order axioms); Menger & Urysohn (curve theory); later Ward, Adeleke–Neumann, Bowditch (pretrees/betweenness)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology / 'formes' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the axioms themselves are unpublished

ideas.what: Divisibility condition (nonempty interior), giving infinitude of segments
Uniqueness of a sub-segment with prescribed endpoints (Cor. 3), segments determined by their endpoints within a segment
ideas.modern_name: uniquely arcwise connected / interval determined by endpoints

missed.claim: A number-free synthetic definition of 'forme 1-dimensionnelle' (places + segments, with branches and order of points and a specialisation relation toward singular places) was begun as the foundational layer of Grothendieck's 1986 geometry of forms. It was not developed into a theory reconstructing graphs or tame curves.
missed.quote: Modèle d'une forme 1-dimensionnelle ... L, ensemble des "lieux" ... S, "segments"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to tame/o-minimal topology and to betweenness/pretree axiomatics. That literature does not tie in the scheme-like specialisation from interior places to singular places, which could suit a combinatorial (finite-space/poset) model of 1-dimensional stratified spaces. The interest is modest, as most individual axioms are classical.

deep.surprise_reason: Early, routine axiomatic groundwork (betweenness-style axioms for segments) with easy corollaries. Historically interesting as part of the unpublished 'géométrie des formes', but the mathematics itself is close to classical order and dendrite axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 is the page number '4', and the title reads 'Modèle d'une forme 1-dimensionnelle' (correct).
In the definition of Ĩ, the gloss reads '(Ĩ, ens. des lieux sur le segment I)'. The second gloss reads '(∂I, ens. des deux lieux extrémités de I)'; 'extrémités' is underlined.

Before 'Cor. 3a' the struck word is 'Alors' followed by a struck abbreviation. The image line reads 'Alors a) cette application est injective, b) Son image contient les ε ∈ P_2(Ĩ) tels que ε ∩ ∂I ≠ ∅'.
The vertical left-margin note beside the bracketed F1 statement is hard to read. 'axiome de connexité' is uncertain; it might refer to uniqueness/existence of sub-segments.
The rotated margin note near the cancelled F2 reads approximately '(F.r.) Faire ... ∀a ∈ Ĩ° ... condition de divisibilité'. It is linked by the asterisk to Cor. 1*.
